steps.body: When two addends are equal, start with the double you already know, then join the third addend.
steps.narration: When two addends are equal, start with the double you already know, then join the third addend.

widget.prompt: The double 4 + 4 lands on 8. Now join 3 more.
widget.missFeedback: Start at 8 and count on 3: you land on 11.
widget.successFeedback: Landed on 11 — the double gave 8 instantly, and joining 3 finished the total.

predict.prompt: Two addends are both 5. Which fact starts fastest?
predict.reveal: A known double is instant; counting from zero re-does work you already know: reaching 10 from zero takes ten separate counts, while 5 + 5 = 10 is one remembered fact.

options.label: Any order — all three are small
options.feedback: Correct — with three small addends no grouping is clearly faster, so any order is fine.

options.label: Only left to right is allowed
options.feedback: Addition permits any grouping; left-to-right is a habit, not a rule.

options.label: Make ten first
options.feedback: These addends are too small to reach ten as a pair, so there is no ten to make.

options.label: Use a double
options.feedback: A double only helps when two addends are equal, which is not guaranteed here.
